entries.title: On a Windows PC, a crewmate's big build no longer waits while processors sit idle
entries.body: When a crewmate declares a big build or check, it waits in that computer's line until there is room. On a Windows PC a run that had started kept its whole declared processor count against the line until it finished, so the next run waited even while processors sat idle. A running run now counts by what the computer measures once it has started, as on a Mac or Linux computer, so the next run starts sooner.
entries.noPicture: A waiting run starts sooner; nothing on screen looks different while it waits or runs.
